Nintendo Switch 2 Patent Paves Way For DS/Wii U Games

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A latest set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.
  • The Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide.
  • It has been revealed that one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen issue may have been revealed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A latest set of Nintendo patents has been discovered that have paved the way for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to return on Switch 2, so long as the player doesn’t mind shelling out for extra hardware.

The Nintendo DS was a massively popular system, selling 154 million units worldwide. However, the system’s dual-screen design has made it hard for its titles to be rereleased on modern systems. Konami managed it with the Castlevania series, but few other companies seem interested in reviving their DS games on the Switch or Switch 2.

It has been revealed that one possible solution to Nintendo’s second screen issue may have been revealed. According to RetroDodo, two patents have been discovered that will allow the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 to play games from the previous console generations.

According to recent reports, the first patent allows a game to be instantly transferred between two systems, while the second allows a different console to be used alongside one running a title, with the ability to use touchscreen controls. Taken together, these patents could emulate the Nintendo DS, 3DS, and Wii U GamePad.

The caveat is that it would require someone to own two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games. This would be fine in a household that owns both systems, but for those who don’t, it’s an expensive proposition just to be able to run DS, 3DS, and Wii U titles.

This isn’t the first time Nintendo has brought dual-screen games to consoles; DS games were available on the Wii U, with the GamePad used as the bottom screen. This isn’t the most elegant of solutions, especially as it forces the player to keep switching perspective between screens, but it gets the job done.

The caveat to these patents is that it would require someone owning two Nintendo Switch 2 units, or one of each Switch console, to run old games.

It has been revealed that there’s also the question of what games fans would even want to play on such a setup. The obvious answer is the Pokémon games, as fans would crawl through broken glass for modern ports of Pokémon HeartGold & SoulSilver that don’t cost hundreds of dollars on eBay. However, considering Game Freak seems averse to making money, there are still easier-to-port Pokémon games that aren’t on the Switch 2, and the DS games would take a ton of work to enhancement.

The Wii U also doesn’t have much, since pretty much all its best games are already on the Switch, and they received updated ports over the console’s lifespan. Sure, it’d be cool for Nintendo Land to return, but no one’s lining up for Star Fox Zero. The Wii U was such a bomb that Nintendo is unlikely to bring up its ghost, even through a costly hardware expansion.

Sources indicate that the Nintendo 3DS had a stacked library of amazing games, but some of them would lose the system's substantial selling point: 3D visuals. Super Mario 3D Land was a tremendous game, but it requires playing in 3D to get the full effect, especially for its stage secrets. The lack of Streepass and Spotpass would also take away a lot of the extra functions present in Nintendo 3DS games.

It’s entirely possible that these Nintendo Switch 2 patents won’t come to anything. After all, companies patent ideas all the time that never get made. The ability to play DS, 3DS, and Wii U games on the Switch 2 would be incredible, but the price of entry might be a bit too high for most fans, even if the titles are released for free on Nintendo Switch Online.

Sources indicate that godLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

According to recent reports, godLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

Industry observers note that south Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

Sources indicate that the qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not stated why it made the change.

It has been revealed that the UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

Sources indicate that godLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

Patch 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:.

The original article continues below.

As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a latest set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is presently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

Industry observers note that the open test was largely well-received, and players actually highlighted up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

Sources indicate that in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially introduced, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

According to recent reports, numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

According to recent reports, indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game presently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The industry-shaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6 has overshadowed just about everything else going on in the gaming world right now, but one area that has suffered the most seems to be the efforts of the union trying to form a partnership with Rockstar's employees.

While some developers with the studio have been trying for months or even longer to get the initiative off the ground to protect their employee rights, the latest results shared by the IWGB union on Instagram show that there's still a lot more work to be done.

According to reports from sources like the Video Games Chronicle, a vast majority of Rockstar employees voted against the deal that would have seen IWGB representing them as the studio's official union, which turned out to be roughly 75%, or about 1,200 out of the 1,600 employees that participated in the vote against it.

While IWGB has had plenty of support leading up to the official vote, which ran from November 12 to November 26, several current Rockstar employees have already been expressing exactly why they think the vote failed, or why they voted no in the first place.

With statements like how "many of us had legitimate concerns that couldn't be answered fully by the IWGB" or dozens of others expressing how their "time at Rockstar has been amazing" with some of the "best working conditions I could possibly dream of," the vote had a lot going against it already.

The main problem many Rockstar employees had with the vote wasn't the concept of a union representing and protecting them itself, but more so the IWGB specifically, which several responses pointed out how they "failed to provide any practical advantages" and made several campaign claims that didn't accurately represent what it was actually like to work at Rockstar during the creation of GTA 6.

The timing of the vote couldn't have been worse either, as while the IWGB was using the release of GTA 6 to provide more attention to their initiative, several Rockstar employees have previously stated they didn't want to take away from the efforts of the developers that worked so hard on the project, or wanted to reap the success of the launch rather than put it at risk over more unsteady union conflicts.

Despite the current results of the vote, however, the IWGB Game Workers union isn't giving up on Rockstar by any means, as they are using the smaller portion of success to "double down" on their efforts and individual representation for Rockstar employees who opt into their organization, as opposed to moving the whole workforce into it.

Industry News: Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • It has been revealed that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

It has been revealed that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

Sources indicate that it's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

It has been revealed that every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The prayers of Final Fantasy old heads were finally answered this year with the release of Final Fantasy Resonance, a particularly retro-feeling entry in the franchise. Between the real-time battle system and 2.5D aesthetic, it's a throwback in the best way, and fans embraced it wholeheartedly, so much so, even the devs were surprised.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the action-oriented and 3D Final Fantasy games are wonderful too," Keisuke Nakashima, producer on Resonance, told Game*Spark, as translated by Automaton. "But I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of Final Fantasy they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art.".

According to recent reports, I'm a member of noted corner of the overall fandom. Much as I enjoyed the huge, sleek main entries, my heart yearns for games that look and feel like the SNES installments, but with contemporary flavor. That's what Resonance delivers.

"We figured it was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," Nakashima adds. That's always a good starting point, and the devs figured correctly, although there was some concern over just how much it stood out amid the slate otherwise.

It has been revealed that "I expected opinions on it might be divided," Hiroto Furuya, director of Resonance, commented in the same interview. "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it.".

Industry observers note that you and I both. Fans of the long-running role-playing juggernaut have had plenty to enjoy the last while. Besides Resonance, Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth continued the trilogy's blockbuster redux of the classic game, and Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles resurrected a fan-favorite for modern systems.

Sources indicate that final Fantasy Resonance is itself a top-down remake of aspects of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, a mobile game from 2015. I'm willing to bet most who checked out this version glossed over the original. It's probably safe to get moving on a follow-up that draws from further parts of the narrative in Exvius.

  • Sources indicate that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Sources indicate that today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja stated it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

Recent findings suggest that the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

Sources indicate that the amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Sources indicate that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

Industry observers note that in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

Industry observers note that there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

Upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

Word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a company succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a new XCOM, which is yet to be announced, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development problems, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg said it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Money is more notable in Grand Theft Auto 6 than it ever has been before, with Jason and Lucia having countless opportunities to rake in some much-needed dough and make life in Leonida easier.

In a recent development, just like in GTA 5 and GTA Online, robbing banks is one of the most reliable ways to earn a lot of cash. You won't be able to do so until you unlock a key item, though, so let's get into it.

Industry observers note that if you're brave enough to try and rob a bank or any location with Marked Bills in the early hours of GTA 6, you'll very swiftly learn that it's a bad idea. In a nice bit of realism, stealing Marked Bills will set off a dye pack when you leave the bank, ruining your entire haul and covering Jason or Lucia in paint.

In a recent development, thankfully, there's a way to bypass those annoying dye packs and make robbing banks a viable opportunity. To do so, you'll need to unlock the Dye Pack Jammer, a key item that does exactly what it states on the tin and prevents dye packs from exploding. The Dye Pack Jammer is unlocked during the Credit Check story mission in Chapter 3, which means it's unmissable if you put enough time in.

Industry observers note that chapter 3 is one of GTA 6's longer acts, and it took me around 40 hours to reach Credit Check. Your mileage will vary depending on how fast you're taking things, however.

It has been revealed that credit Check sees Jason and Lucia being tested on their robbing ability and tasked with hitting up a few different locations. It's one of the game's best missions and, once you've beaten it, you'll be able to steal from any location on the map. In fact, the map will even point this out to you by highlighting a bunch of newly introduced opportunities and pointing you in their direction.

It's worth noting, however, that any location with Marked Bills will have higher security and will need to be more carefully planned. The pay day is usually worth it, but just keep that in mind.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto’s reference pie isn’t focused solely on the crime fiction that gave it so much of its texture. The most recent Grand Theft Auto 6 owes plenty to its video game contemporaries, and isn’t afraid to toss some love to the biggest and brightest of the industry throughout the journey.

Amongst these references are two Mario and Luigi-styled caps for Jason and Lucia, found through use of an oddly placed bong and a little bit of platforming. If you want some goofy merch to match with your partner in crime, look no further!

To locate the hats, head towards the bottom left corner of Moreau, south of Bonanza. Follow the river until you find the ruins of a paper mill, burnt down in some kind of horrible fire. Towards the left side of the ruins, you’ll find a bong sitting on a table, with a prompt to use it.

Industry observers note that once you do, you’ll hear a poof, and a barely visible block will appear above the central pillar making up the ruins above you. Parkour up the table, and climb between the pillars until you have a clear shot at the block. Shoot it, and two caps will drop on the pillar, one for Jason and one for Lucia.

Make sure you bring both partners to pick them up, and don’t forget to hit the nearby Meditation spot for a nice little boost to your Focus, making this trek both functional and form-efficient. These hats work like any other, throwing cops off your trail if you switch to them before or after committing a crime. Even if wearing your initials on your forehead isn’t exactly the sneakiest option in the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 will soon get a latest enhancement to resolve a number of complications, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it looks to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

Sources indicate that you can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most vital is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis noted this will work with upcoming and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

According to recent reports, you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a upcoming lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

According to recent reports, catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently unveiled that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#212518. Latest Update: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1691 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • It has been revealed that it wasn't ever thus.
  • Industry observers note that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It has been revealed that it wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

Industry observers note that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Fresh York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

Sources indicate that the pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something newly introduced," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty promptly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The big project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

It has been revealed that rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Sources indicate that agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

Industry observers note that while never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij said. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

Recent findings suggest that as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Sources indicate that needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

It has been revealed that "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek – the one behind the likes of Half-Life 2, Portal and its sequel, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, and even Counter-Strike: Global Offensive – thinks GTA 6 is great… because you choose how to play. A fact that's lost on players complaining about optional missions.

Sources indicate that the new Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date. However, there's still a vocal (minority, I'd like to think) group of players dismissing it as a game that forces some sort of agenda upon you. Faliszek covers this in his YouTube video on the "moral yellow paint," so to speak, of GTA 6.

According to the Valve veteran, there's no real reason for folks to complain about menial tasks like painting the house as Jason or buying flowers, even if "the game indicates you're getting some kind of points or… gives you this list.".

While other games use yellow paint to give you set boundaries to stay within, in GTA 6 you can stray in whatever direction you'd like and play how you wish.

According to recent reports, in Faliszek's case, that means, uh, "bringing back bodies" and filling the house with corpses. It's all just GTA, after all.

"Now, would I do that in normal life? Does that make me a horrible person? Maybe. Does that make me a psycho in the game? Who cares?" As he says, "This is Grand Theft Auto." So, go on and ditch the chores to commit mass murder (if you please, of course). The writer notes that, again, it's all part of the game's sandbox elements – and, on that point, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 such a stand-out release.

In a separate short, Faliszek dubs GTA 6 "a masterpiece," saying, "it may be the greatest game ever made." He references other devs' criticism of Rockstar's new title – such as Warren Spector's, which argues he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – and dismisses it, reiterating that "it's an amazing game" and "incredible." I'm sure the freedom (to collect bodies, apparently) is a big reason why.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

So, share in Faliszek's sentiment here and don't box yourself in with any preconceived "yellow paint" in GTA 6 when you don't have to. Clean the house, shower, buy gifts… or wreak havoc in Vice City and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours.

Last night, The Game Awards 2026 nominations were officially declared, and fans immediately noticed the prestigious Game of the Year category - previously won by the likes of Astro Bot, Clair Obscur, and Elden Ring - does not feature a PlayStation-published game this year. It's a rare sight for PlayStation Studios, which has secured a Game of the Year nomination every year since 2015.

PlayStation has published several games this year that might usually be shoe-ins for a Game of the Year nomination. Marvel's Wolverine is the manufacturer's highest profile first-party release in 2026, but it's also responsible for this year's Saros, as well as the externally-developed but PlayStation-published Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls.

Despite missing out on the Game of the Year slot, however, PlayStation still features in other categories. All three of the aforementioned games are up for various, non-GOTY awards, while Marathon is nominated for Best Multiplayer, and the upcoming God of War Laufey for Most Anticipated. Here's all of PlayStation's 2026 nominations:.

And if you're wondering, here are the 13 Game of the Year nominations PlayStation has secured over the last 11 years:.

2027's PlayStation slate of games might fare better at next year's The Game Awards, what with a upcoming entry in the often-nominated God of War series in Laufey, and potentially Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Recent findings suggest that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

Recent findings suggest that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

In a recent development, it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

Recent findings suggest that and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robberies are one of the most important aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay loop, and they can be quite difficult if you don't approach them carefully and with a bit of planning.

Industry observers note that in the early game, Jason and Lucia are small-time criminals who make their lack of experience known, but you can quickly turn them into stealthy professionals by unlocking a key item. Here's what to do.

Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida has a surprising number of buildings that the player can actually enter, and many of them are teeming with robbery opportunities. In the early hours of the game, however, most buildings are very difficult to quietly enter, as locked doors prevent Jason and Lucia from doing whatever they please.

According to recent reports, at first, your only choice for locked doors is to noisily break them open, which draws a lot of attention and makes stealth a no-go in most cases. That changes when you unlock the Snap Gun, which lets you pick the lock of any door in the game and gain access to locations without making a sound.

Like several helpful items in GTA 6, the Snap Gun is given to you as part of the main story, although it's a little more involved than others. To start with, you'll need to complete Chapter 3's Boobie Time mission, which will introduce you to Yasmani, a fence who specialises in jewellery. Yasmani will call you after the mission and task you with completing three jewellery store heists.

Once you complete any one of those three missions and return to Yasmani, he'll give you the Snap Gun as a reward. This device unlocks a latest option for locked doors, as you can now choose to use the Snap Gun to unlock them through a minigame that's similar to hotwiring. You'll need to find the sweet spot with the left stick and hit R2 on PlayStation or RT on Xbox to pick the door, which adds a whole new layer to robberies.

The Snap Gun's minigame is unique since you can really just point anywhere and quickly mash R2/RT without any trouble.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a week of GTA 6's availability, there are two things I can say with complete certainty: first, Red Dead Redemption 2 is the best thing that could have happened to Rockstar, and second, we'll be following Jason, Lucia, and company for a long time.

The developer's magnum opus offers an immersive and expansive world that will take us many years to fully decipher, so I can already imagine how numerous ecosystems, from video games to content creation, will be completely permeated until, perhaps, the release of the seventh installment.

However, far from wanting to theorize about future adventures of the IP, the priority is to appreciate the one we already have in our hands and savor it slowly, since that's what the game itself aims for by offering a story, mechanics, and context that evolve at a much more leisurely pace.

Therefore, in order to play fortune teller and anticipate how long we will be hanging around Leonida, I invite you to read this list of ten reasons you will be playing GTA 6 for more than a decade.

Analyzing the evolution of video games, especially considering their affinity with technology, is an activity that involves intertemporal comparisons, and GTA 6 has established itself as the generational benchmark we look to when we want to see if the industry has moved forward.

Titles like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, BioShock, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, and The Last of Us Part II have stood for years as monoliths of their respective genres and platforms, garnering enduring attention that regularly draws us back to reaffirm their influence.

Thus, considering the technical, graphical, and design marvel that is Rockstar's title, particularly within the context of open worlds, it will be impossible for it to escape associations with future representatives of the genre, who will undoubtedly seek to learn from it.

Although comparisons are generally odious, it's also true that they constitute a timely method to contrast the evolution, or involution, of a medium, so I can already see many scholars of this art revisiting its confines to diagnose its eventual state.

While I acknowledge the omnipresence of the internet and our hyper-connected state has made the task of hunting for secrets virtually impossible, I know I'm not the only one who has deliberately avoided all discussion about the game in order to discover it for myself.

By choosing not to use guides, watch gameplay videos, or even compare opinions, the game's lifespan is instantly extended due to its immeasurable size and content, much of which is hidden behind hundreds of hours of spontaneous and meticulous exploration.

You may finish the campaign and feel satisfied with what you've experienced, but for a game that has taken so long to arrive and generated so much anticipation, I'm sure that a large portion of its player base will continue playing until there's no dialogue, NPC, mission, weapon, or random event left undiscovered.

This largely depends on how much you choose to interact with its online discourse, as you will surely encounter spoilers of all kinds as the days and months go by, yet a whole second life awaits you if you choose to turn a blind eye to other people's experiences and strive to discover everything on your own.

Assuming I'm not the only oddball who's spent countless hours wandering around open-world games listening to their tunes without engaging in any particular activity, GTA 6's deep and outstanding soundtrack will behave like a music player with extra steps.

In fact, a large part of my GTA 5 playtime consisted of countless nights spent hopping into any legitimately acquired vehicle and cruising around the city's interiors and exteriors, and after just an hour of playing this new installment, I already knew the future would be the same.

Whether you enjoy pop, urban music, rap, or listening to the radio as if it were real life (which it is closer to than I'd like to admit), there's a station for every type of listener, helping the game also become an album that will remind you of the era in which it was released.

Never underestimate the power of songs as tools to prolong our connection with a video game because, just like with Secunda in Skyrim or I Really Want To Stay at Your House in Cyberpunk 2077, I'm sure RHYNO will have us going around in circles in Vice City for a very, very long time.

A major surprise I encountered in my first few hours of playing GTA 6 was the influence of immersive sims on its mission design, as there isn't just one way to solve many of the main and side objectives in the campaign.

Obviously, we're not talking about the depth of an Arkane Studios title, though there's enough density and player agency to allow for diverse approaches, ranging from peaceful resolutions if you know who to talk to, to stealthy sieges where no one necessarily has to be killed.

Add to that the game's inherent spontaneity, which throws you into special and unexpected encounters every second, all waiting to grab your attention, and you realize its replayability stems from a design specifically intended to be open and multifaceted.

I hope GTA 6's approach helps the genre emerge from its slumber, but while I invoke every possible deity to make that happen, I'm content to return to Leonida every few years to see what newly introduced interactions Rockstar prepared without me noticing in my first five playthroughs.

In conjunction with the above, the title places a notable emphasis on role-playing elements, influencing both the story and gameplay according to how the player chooses to interact with their world, allowing Jason and Lucia to be canvases with clear forms yet ultimately emphasized by the player.

Between choosing the type of relationship they develop, making choices that influence the narrative at key plot points, and the constant decision-making involved in adhering to (or not) morality and law, you can have completely different experiences if you shift your mindset enough.

It has been revealed that in this sense, for my first playthrough, I have a more restrained and rigorous Jason and a more antisocial and rebellious Lucia within a loving relationship, always acting in accordance with these personality archetypes. Regardless, for my second playthrough, I plan to take a completely opposite path.

In a recent development, the result? At the very least, one more run with hundreds of hours and variations that will make me even more amazed by the immeasurable talent of the Rockstar workers, to whom I feel I owe the respect of playing the game at least three times to properly appreciate the countless hours they invested in shaping the product.

The third of my three planned playthroughs, designed to fully exploit the game, will consist of not killing anyone unless the game forces me to, which brings us to the mechanism that has kept hundreds of video games alive online: challenge runs.

In a recent development, beating the entire game with only fists, without breaking any laws, without using money, with only a knife, using only public transport, in the shortest time feasible, as the worst possible partner... I don't know if the possibilities are truly infinite, but they certainly come close.

Games like Dark Souls and Hollow Knight have demonstrated for years that human creativity knows no bounds, especially when it comes to creating content that borders on masochism, so it's only natural that GTA 6 will be like a second home for all these inventive people.

I don't know if I'll be among them, yet my experience being chronically online assures me with complete certainty that GTA 6 will sustain entire communities based on challenges, rising exponentially if mods are added to the equation.

Heraclitus said it's impossible to step into the same river twice because everything changes, both in the river itself and in the person crossing it, and I believe the mythical Greek philosopher made this aphorism with the belief that we would eventually have the boundless body of water that is GTA 6.

Experiences with open worlds, like the aforementioned Skyrim or, more recently, Elden Ring, tend to be special thanks to the organic nature of their worlds, given you feel like you're in an alternate, digital reality where you're truly part of a larger cosmos.

Leonida, however, takes these sensations to uncharted territory, where it genuinely feels impossible to experience the same thing twice because of how reactive and multifaceted its systems are, like hundreds of thousands of windows that only open if you're in the right place at the right time.

This contextual fertility ensures that there will almost always be a new experience to go through, and as long as the flame of belief that there are unexplored horizons remains alive (something that GTA 5 already demonstrated), there will be parishioners who remain absorbed watching the fire, waiting to hear an unprecedented crackle.

The fear of missing out on a cultural event is fascinating because, contrary to popular belief, it can have a timeless quality; for example, it's the reason I played the first iterations of Red Dead Redemption and The Last of Us, even though it was a decade after their respective releases.

Given GTA 6 is and will be a cultural touchstone of modern entertainment, many will return to its realm years later to satisfy a curiosity they perhaps didn't solve at launch for one reason or another, ranging from waiting for a price drop to the complete optimization of its features.

Beyond the causes, and considering a legacy that is already titanic after just one week of release and will become even more staggering as time goes on, it seems that playing GTA 6 will be like watching The Godfather or reading the Odyssey: an essential ritual for understanding the path its medium will take in the future.

Even if you're not a fan of the series or the genre, the curiosity to understand the reasons behind its multi-million sales and resounding unanimous praise as a masterpiece on Metacritic will be compelling for those who value video games as an art form, since great works always deserve attention, even if it's to criticize them.

Rockstar has found its closest model to follow in GTA 5, the same recipe that allowed them to maintain the product's relevance for over ten years with virtually no significant drop in popularity or impact, whose success hinges on spacing out re-releases, which will rekindle the unresolved desires of a significant portion of the gaming community.

Motivated by the release of the PC version and potential upcoming consoles from Microsoft and Sony, or even by the anticipation of a product with as few bugs and inconsistencies as possible, many people will refrain from jumping on the bandwagon at its peak, instead patiently waiting for the waters to calm down.

The 235 million copies sold of its predecessor didn't happen overnight; they materialized gradually and steadily year after year, and it's quite easy to predict that market behavior this time around will be virtually the same.

Many of them are repeat buyers, of course, but that doesn't invalidate the title's statement: whether it's your first time or your fiftieth, the hardware will give you very appealing reasons to discover or check out how GTA 6 is, even if it's 2036.

However, by far, the biggest reason to be sure you'll be playing GTA 6 for more than ten years lies in its multiplayer mode, a fundamental pillar that sustained GTA 5 throughout its lifespan and which, without a doubt, will repeat that feat with this fresh installment.

If we assume Rockstar will be able to create a product that surpasses its predecessor as the base game did, the only sensible conclusion about the next iteration of GTA Online is that it will be a candidate for the most massive, complex, and profitable multiplayer experience of all time.

Phenomena like Fortnite or League of Legends cast doubt on such a claim, but the fact that this is even the scale used to measure GTA 6's multiplayer is indicative enough of what it will mean for the franchise and the market once it's released.

More than the sheer scale of its world, more than sociocultural pressure, and more than even any traditional DLC, what could allow Rockstar to go two generations without releasing a game and still be the most popular developer in the world is the online variant of GTA 6.

Not only because of its name and legacy, which also mean a great deal, but because of the game's inherent quality, which suggests that its size, freedom of action, and overall quality will be remarkable enough to carry the Grand Theft Auto name for as long as it lasts.

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

It has been revealed that to top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

Recent findings suggest that I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

Industry observers note that according to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in Newly introduced Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

According to recent reports, the previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 launches officially in more regions of the world.

Industry observers note that if you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. You can also read the Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 guide for a full breakdown on all the details ahead of its launch in your region.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Sources indicate that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Recent findings suggest that once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the upcoming Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

Sources indicate that the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big fresh update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

Warren Spector: "I don't think you can look at Zelda: Breath of the Wild and not see Deus Ex"

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that plenty of people would have told you that the real-time strategy game began to 'die out' in the late 2000s, a once-mighty genre that no longer interested modern audiences. But the more nuanced version of that narrative is that the RTS evolved, various core ideas stripped of their outside complexities before being expanded into their own genres. Without Warcraft 3, for instance, there wouldn't have been a League of Legends or Dota 2. Now, a leading figure behind another 'dying' genre indicates that its DNA is simply to be found elsewhere - primarily within the RPG.

Speaking to Edge, legendary immersive sim designer Warren Spector stated that "the heart of the immersive sim has kind of been adopted by mainstream gaming." Best known for series like Thief, System Shock, Ultima, and Deus Ex, Spector is widely considered a major force in the development of the entire imsim genre, and that influence is a major personal marker of success.

"One of my egomaniacal success criteria was to have influence. I've always wanted to try, even if I fail, to change things." His argument, however, is that he has very much not failed to change things, and that the ideas that were once the individual domain of the immersive sim are now found much further afield.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't think you can look at Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom and not see a little bit of Deus Ex in it," he states. "And I think roleplaying games now are far more immersive sim-y than they used to be, going further to empower players to tell their own stories." While the two Zelda titans are obvious examples, other RPGs have also done work to deserve that mantle - Baldur's Gate 3 is a particularly good example of the imsim's systems-driven heritage, and a lot of what we're hearing about GTA 6 implies that some of its big ideas - particularly its Wanted system - will be very immersive.

The result, for Spector, is that a trace of the old self exists in the new self. Even if immersive sims aren't a driving force in the industry right now, he says, "I don't know that we're dead. I think we're like a parasite that's invaded the body. And that's all you can ask for. Making games different and better and more what they should be, and empowering players to become authors - that's all I ever wanted to do, and now there are lots of people doing that, even if they don't realise they are.".

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

Industry observers note that the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A upcoming Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major enhancement. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

Recent findings suggest that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the massive focus of this enhancement, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

It has been revealed that the hot latest arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

According to recent reports, in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Industry observers note that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

It has been revealed that version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a newly introduced activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.
